content:
jamie: Heads up — after we cordoned a subset of GPU nodes in eu-west1 for onboarding, apiserver started showing a large spike in watch reconnects and 503s around 20:02 UTC. Anyone seeing context?

oncall-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2026-042 (apiserver watch surge) — paging eng-sre.

ravi: Looking at the control-plane logs: etcd WAL fsync latency jumped hard at 20:01. nvme i/o queue depth on the provisioner hosts spiked. Snippet: 
```
etcdserver: apply entries timeout, wal sync took 52ms
grpc: failed to send, i/o timeout
apiserver: watch fanout backlog 1124 -> 4300
```

claire: We cordoned ~12 gpus to onboard the new batch model cache. Drains used `kubectl drain --delete-local-data`. Were there any heavy local-disk jobs running during drains?

jamie: Yes — model-cache warmup init-containers run a parallel download + extraction to local NVMe. We expected low concurrency but looks like the provisioner triggered multiple warmups at once during the cordon.

maria: Spinning up iostat/dstat traces now and linking grafana panel (https://grafana.company/r/ctrlplane-iops). Will paste numbers in a sec.

ravi: From node metrics: nvme avg write latency jumped ~1ms -> 45ms, avg queue length hit ~180 for ~90s. etcd WAL queue backed up, leader observed >10s election jitter and controller-manager restarted once due to lease renew failures.

claire: That explains the leader-election churn and controller restarts. When controller-manager restarts it re-acquires leases and we get watch replays which amplifies apiserver fanout.

jamie: Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Uncordon 3 nodes in a staggered fashion to relieve i/o pressure.
2) Scale down model-warmup jobs by 80% for the next 10m.
3) Put provisioner into limited-concurrency mode (throttle new onboarding work).

devops: Uncordoned 2 nodes just now (eu-west1-gpu-07, -08). Observability: apiserver watch backlog dropped from ~1400 -> ~420 within 30s.

maria: Filed PR #4123 to provisioner that adds jittered delays between warmup tasks and a concurrency cap per-provisioner. Also adding a tape-out config to mark disk-heavy init containers so they can be rate-limited.

ravi: Longer-term actions: lower kubelet eviction thresholds for local-disk pressure on GPU fleets, consider moving warmup downloads to tmpfs (if memory allows) or to a shared caching service to avoid bursty NVMe writes during scale events. Also we should add WAL fsync SLO alarms on etcd nodes.

jamie: I'll start a postmortem draft and include cost/ops notes — NVMe IO spikes hit us on IO credits and caused extra retries which increased control-plane token counts.

oncall-bot: Incident severity lowered to P2.

claire: TL;DR: cordon + concurrent local-disk warmups -> NVMe i/o saturation on provisioners -> etcd WAL latency -> leader election churn -> controller-manager restart -> apiserver watch fanout spike. Fixes: throttle warmups, stagger cordons, add disk pressure evictions, add WAL latency alert. :thumbsup:

jamie: Agree. I'll sync with infra tomorrow to bake the throttle into the onboarding runbook. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
